sources.name: Drilling Permits Issued for Development and for Exploratory (Wildcat) Wells in Nebraska, 1975 to 2025 (state energy statistics, two PDFs)
sources.license: Public state statistics; cites the commission's Nebraska Oil Activity Summary
sources.tested: Page 200 (updated May 7, 2026; 'typically one year between updates'). Development PDF 200, 75 KB: an annual table 2010 to 2029 (2020: 8, 2021: 26, 2022: 46, 2023: NA, 2024: 15, 2025: 8; later years NA) and monthly counts by year for 1977 to 2014 only (2014 has only January and February). The page text gives exploratory permits as 13 in 2024 and 9 in 2025. Counts mix crude oil and natural gas wells. Peak 1981: 374 development and 354 exploratory.

sources.name: NebraskaNEW feature service, layer NE_WELLS (FracTracker Alliance's copy of commission well data; third party)
sources.license: Copyright text names FracTracker Alliance; underlying data is the commission's
sources.tested: Layer ?f=json 200 (query only, maxRecordCount 1000, no last-edit date). Statistics query: 16,084 wells, of which 13,119 dry holes, 1,834 oil/gas, 475 enhanced-recovery injection, 321 natural gas, 140 water injection/disposal, 109 gas storage, 39 stratigraphic, 38 water source, and a few geothermal, storage and class I wells. No date fields at all, so it cannot give permit counts. A static snapshot of unknown age; not the agency's file.

grade_reason: The commission's host reset every connection from here, so its permit-by-year files, wells shapefile and Access database could not be seen (they are reported to exist and be free). The reachable fragments are annual and monthly permit counts from the state energy office (monthly only to 2014, 2023 missing) and a third-party well layer with no dates. Nebraska issued only 17 development and exploratory permits in 2025 (28 in 2024), so it is a very small state. Could rise to A or B if the yearly permit files carry approval dates and a GitHub runner can reach them.
producer_plan: Today: use the state energy office's two PDFs, which give permits issued per year (development plus exploratory, oil and gas together) for 1975 to 2025, and per month through 2014; they are refreshed about once a year in May, and 2023 is NA. That supports an annual 'new wells permitted' line only. Next step before building anything: from a GitHub Actions runner, make one request each for the commission's Data and Publications page, the drilling permit file for the latest year, and the wells shapefile; a refusal from there is an answer and the state stays a statistics line. If the yearly permit files open and carry an approval date, count rows per month (Form 2 is 'drill or re-enter', so a work-type column may split new from re-entry); if they do not, the Access well database may hold permit and spud dates. The FracTracker copy has no dates and should not be a source. Caveats: tiny counts (about 8 to 46 a year), a long lag in the annual figures, and no injection or amendment bands known.
privacy_notes: Not checked: no agency rows were seen. The mirror's Co_Name column names companies; whether any are individuals was not inspected. Form 2 asks for operator contact details and a signature, and a plat, which would show private land; publish company names and counts only.
